thesis: Small H1 earnings deterioration supports relative resilience, but the income thesis and the bearish capital objection both depend on unextracted bank metrics. Neither demonstrates an adequately valued income purchase or an observed credit impairment. Dividend growth is a distribution fact, not capital validation.
strongest_counterexample: Q2 profit improved and the interim dividend rose to 31 sen, while H1 profit declined only approximately 0.9%, supporting a substantial resilient income base.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable half-year reports attributable profit growth above zero, maintains at least the observed 31 sen interim distribution, and documents compliance with applicable capital/liquidity requirements without worsening asset quality, resolving the core income gates.
A distribution cut below 31 sen or disclosed breach of applicable capital/liquidity requirements would invalidate the retained income-resilience scenario.
evidence_gaps: CET1, asset quality, credit costs, liquidity and funding spreads.
Recurring-income/distribution coverage and matched bank valuation.
decisive_factors: Price below both averages with negative MACD; OPR stability does not establish NIM expansion.
